text: Hello everyone. Ladies and gentlemen,
this afternoon we are witnessing a wave
of crisis and riots in Iran. The reason
is that the people of Iran are very
hungry. They no longer have enough food
to eat. Therefore, they are no longer
afraid of death. If they are not afraid
of death, the Islamic Republic of Iran
government can no longer threaten to
kill them. That is why they have risen
up. I have summarized that the crisis
in Iran is truly very serious. Small
businesses can no longer trade because
the policies of the Islamic Republic of
Iran are too extreme. That is why young
people are now rising up. Let us take a
look at all the developments happening
in Iran right now. This is the scene of
Iranian shopkeepers having to close
down because they cannot trade anymore.
It is because the Islamic Republic of
Iran government cuts off power without
notifying them. As a result, these
goods, such as meat and fresh produce,
have gone bad. These are all very
expensive items because Iran is in
crisis and the currency has devalued.
Therefore, this is all of their
property. But when the goods are lost,
they lose both their capital and their
profit. Previously, they relied on this
livelihood to make a living, but now
they can no longer earn enough money to
feed their families. We have updates
from inside Iran, where they say there
is no electricity in the hot summer,
and goods worth a fortune. They have
been spoiled and ruined. The Islamic
Republic of Iran government cannot even
inform its citizens when the power will
be cut. Sometimes they even proactively
cut the power, causing refrigerators,
freezers, and televisions to break; no
one takes responsibility, and no one is
compensated. With everything that the
Islamic Republic of Iran government has
brought upon its people, the people
have begun to rise up. You can see the
young people of Iran trampling on
police cars to destroy them. This video
features the lion and sun flag, meaning
support for Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi,
along with the posting date of the 4th.
However, at this moment, I still cannot
confirm the exact time and location
where this event took place. But many
other events have happened
simultaneously; here are long lines of
people waiting for gasoline everywhere.
They say that this is one of the
wealthiest nations in terms of oil and
natural gas. However, after the 1979
Islamic Revolution, today, 45 years
later, Iran has turned into a tragedy
like this. Even the large supermarkets,
which were once the busiest shopping
centers in the heart of Tehran, or in
other major cities, as you can see, are
completely deserted. There are a few
scattered stalls open, but there are no
customers coming in or out. Because at
this point, the people have no money
left. With such hyperinflation, they
cannot even afford simple basic
necessities. How could they have money
to enter large supermarkets like these?
This video was released by Iran
International. Perhaps an Iranian
citizen filmed it and then secretly
sent it to Iran International, a media
outlet based in London. They say that
this is a shopping center in the
capital, Tehran. The stalls are very,
very empty; in some places, there is
not a single soul to be seen. With all
that crisis and social instability, the
Iranian people are finding ways to rise
up, especially the young. You can see
their courage. They are hanging the
flag of the former Persian Empire. This
means they do not accept following the
path of the Islamic Republic or this
extreme clerical regime. They have
experienced 45 years, and that is more
than enough. Therefore, the young
people are hanging the flag of the
Persian Empire out on the streets. This
video was just released yesterday, the
4th, showing that young Iranians
everywhere have begun to spark an
uprising. Now, who has the courage to
provide them with weapons and organize
them? That is the key question. As for
their bravery, it is already on display
here. Thus, we can see that President
Trump has already come one step closer
to victory in Iran. But it is just that
left-wing media outlets are still
finding every way to oppose Trump.
President Trump recently posted an
article saying that extreme leftists
would rather accept America losing than
accept President Trump winning. It
means their personal feelings toward
President Trump are just too strong.
Therefore, they would rather see
America lose than let President Trump
win. However, President Trump says that
the Iran issue does not deserve to be
called a full-scale war. It can only be
considered a minor conflict. It is just
like a small potato that the U.S. can
handle without needing to deploy its
full forces. Here we can also see a
contrasting picture if we compare the
U.S. and Russia. President Putin is
holding Russia back, while Trump is
elevating America's status very high. I
have compiled some evidence here to
point out this contrast and
simultaneously refute arguments from
many influential voices. They say that
the personal relationship between Trump
and Putin; I do not agree with that
argument. Here we have many voices from
the most famous figures in the world,
especially regarding Russia's attack on
the center of the capital, Kyiv, ahead
of the visit by Jared Kushner and Steve
Witkoff to Kyiv. In the past, when U.S.
dignitaries visited the two capitals of
Moscow and Kyiv, both sides would not
attack. This time, Kyiv has not
attacked Moscow for several days now,
but Moscow has attacked Kyiv. This
proves that the arguments claiming
President Trump is Putin's puppet or
follows Putin's orders are wrong.
Recently, many people have compared
U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian
President Vladimir Putin, saying they
have many similarities and some even
say President Trump is Putin's puppet.
But today, I will bring you the
perspectives coming from the citizens
of both countries. On the other side,
represented by the tycoon Mikhail
Khodorkovsky. He says that Putin is
taking Russia back to the darkest
periods of the Soviet Union, leaving
Russia lagging behind history. On this
side, we have history professor Victor
Davis Hanson. He says that Trump is
taking the U.S. to the highest position
on the international stage. First, we
have an experience coming from ordinary
Russian citizens themselves. They go to
get gas, and those gas stations are no
longer selling to ordinary people. They
only sell by ration coupons, and she
says we are being pushed back to the
darkest times of the Soviet Union.
These are her exact words. Before
heading to work, I decided to stop at a
gas station. I turned into a Rosneft
station. I saw they only had A92
gasoline left. I thought, well, that's
fine, at least I can fill up with 92.
Then they told me they only sell gas
there with ration coupons. I was
stunned, thinking, what on earth is a
ration coupon? An attendant told me
that the coupons are issued to you at
the company or agency where you work. I
just had to reply. Yes, I understand
now. After that, I got into my car, and
you know what? I was feeling a bit
shocked. I mean, buying gas with ration
coupons, guys. With coupons just to buy
gas. What the hell is going on here, I
don't know. At this rate, it won't be
long before we have to buy bread, milk,
eggs, and meat with coupons again.
Greetings from the past, I guess. Now I
will try to go to a Lukoil station to
see if I can fill up. I hope they won't
make me use a ration coupon there too.
Next is a very heartfelt segment shared
by oligarch Mikhail Khodorkovsky. He
recounts the moment he realized Putin
was a butcher, a sick individual. The
exact words the oligarch Khodorkovsky
used were a person with a perverted
personality. In September 2004,
terrorists seized School No. 1 in
Beslan, a town in Southern Russia. They
took about 1,000 children, relatives,
and teachers hostage, demanding Russian
troops withdraw from Chechnya. The
siege lasted for three days. During
that time, students and teachers were
held in cramped, unsanitary conditions,
without water, food, or access to
toilets. State television deliberately
lied to the public, claiming there were
only 350 hostages, even though they
knew full well over 1,100 people were
being forced to drink urine instead of
clean water. This was also a turning
point for Margarita Simonyan, who is
currently the editor-in-chief of RT.
She became famous for her reports on
the attack, and her talent—in
quotation marks—was quickly noticed.
At one point during the crisis, it was
clear that a successful negotiation to
save the children was highly likely
with the mediation of Aslan Maskhadov,
the leader of the Chechen independence
movement. But for Putin, who was
cultivating an image as a young and
dynamic new leader. Engaging in
dialogue with someone like Maskhadov
meant immediate loss of face. So, to
prevent Maskhadov from acting as a
mediator and gaining legitimacy, the
Kremlin ordered a surprise, bloody
assault. It was not a rescue mission,
but a heavy military attack. On Putin's
orders, Russian forces fired
thermobaric weapons directly into the
booby-trapped school building,
triggering explosions and a massive,
deadly fire. At that time, Putin's
military had only one top priority: to
eliminate the terrorists. Saving the
children was second, or perhaps even
lower on the list of priorities. As
soon as the cameras stopped rolling,
support for the survivors was also cut
off. The state had turned their school
into rubble but wouldn't spend a single
ruble to treat their broken bones and
burns. At the time, I had to personally
intervene from my prison cell to
coordinate and fund their
rehabilitation and medical treatment.
Because Putin's federal government had
completely abandoned the people, as if
the bitterness wasn't already enough.
After the parents received this
financial aid, the state even sent them
invoices demanding they pay taxes on
that money. The political shamelessness
at that time was truly staggering.
Putin used the brutal attack on
children as a pretext to abolish the
direct election of regional governors.
Of course, in reality, this proposal
had absolutely nothing to do with
security. The sole reason for canceling
gubernatorial elections was to
dismantle the federal system and secure
Putin's lifelong rule as well as
immunity from criminal prosecution.
Notably, throughout the past two
decades, Putin has never visited Beslan
on the anniversaries of the tragedy.
During key milestones like the 10th and
15th anniversaries, he instead flew to
Mongolia to commemorate a battle from a
century ago. In 2023, he designated a
day in September as the day of victory
over Japan. A new holiday created
solely to erase the pain of the Beslan
people from public memory. Furthermore,
Putin's administration has always
treated grieving families with extreme
cruelty. In 2016, a group called Voice
of Beslan, an organization of mothers
who lost their children, held a public
protest. They wore t-shirts bearing a
brief but painful message. Putin is the
executioner of Beslan. They demanded an
explanation as to why the assault was
carried out in that manner. Instead of
receiving answers, they were arrested,
fined, and sentenced to community
service. And eight years later, for the
20th anniversary in 2024, Putin made a
hurried, televised visit to the town
still steeped in grief. But he was so
unprepared and lacked such empathy that
he stated the wrong number of children
who died right in front of the cameras.
He said 136 children had died, while
the actual figure was 186. He spent the
remaining time lecturing the mothers
about imaginary foreign conspiracies.
And when the mothers asked why the
official investigation had not been
completed after 20 years, Putin replied
that it was his first time hearing
about it and told them to see Bastrykin
, the head of the Russian Investigative
Committee. So his surprise visit after
20 years of silence was nothing more
than a performance to polish his image.
It had a clear purpose: to distract
domestic public opinion from his
serious military failures in the war in
Ukraine. Beslan is clear and horrific
proof that Putin is a sociopath who
views his own citizens as expendable to
serve his power and approval ratings.
If he can do this to his own people, he
can do the same to anyone. Therefore, I
am convinced that the real threat to
global stability is not his departure
from power, but his continued rule.
Next, we will look at what Trump has
done for America and why comparing
Trump to Putin is completely illogical.
The distinguished Harvard history
professor Victor Davis Hanson has said
that if you look at the Russian
Federation, Russia is now just a shadow
of its former self. And if you look at
NATO, the bloc is rearming in a way no
one ever thought was possible. Trump is
bringing America to a position of
supremacy, and the world today has
nothing in common with the world of
five years ago. That could be very bad.
But when you look at it systematically,
objectively, and rationally, you will
see the following. First, let's look at
Venezuela. Is this country exporting
terrorism and drugs to North America?
Absolutely not. On the contrary, we
just signed a deal that will basically
allow the U.S. access to 65 billion
barrels of Venezuelan oil over the next
100 years, which is high-sulfur, very
heavy, but very valuable. Venezuela
will receive 19 dollars no matter what
happens, without spending a cent for
every barrel of oil that U.S. oil
companies try to extract. And if you do
the math, the costs in Venezuela are
not like those in Arabia, nor are they
like those in the U.S. This is not
light sweet crude oil. It is a
difficult place politically. It is a
place that is challenging
geographically and climatically. And it
will cost oil companies between 30 and
40 or 50 dollars. And if oil prices
drop below 65 dollars a barrel, this is
very good for Venezuela. And that is
why they agreed to this deal with the
U.S. But more importantly, the entire
South American region, the entire
Caribbean, and the entire Central
American region have become so
different that they are unrecognizable
compared to five years ago before Joe
Biden took office. There are currently
no issues with the Panama Canal, and
Cuba is struggling. There are only five
governments in the Latin American
region that are anti-American; the vast
majority are capitalist, democratic,
and staunchly pro-American nations. Now
let's move to the Middle East, one of
the biggest problems we have faced in
the Middle East over the past 50 years.
One of the biggest problems is Iran.
But it's not just Iran, it's also their
proxy forces like Hezbollah, Hamas, and
the Houthis. Previously, there wasn't
really a proper nation of Lebanon. The
country had been hijacked by Hezbollah.
You heard the Lebanese Prime Minister
speak a few days ago. He said that this
is the first time there has been a real
opportunity in Lebanon. Why is that?
Because Hezbollah has had its fangs
pulled by Israel. But more importantly,
they have run out of money. Why are
they out of money? Because we are
imposing the strictest sanctions on
Iran that we have ever seen. Even
though we are hearing that Iran is
winning the war, in reality, they are
almost finished. We have used a boa
constrictor-style tightening tactic.
Iran's military has been degraded by
about 90%, but more importantly, they
have no more oil. Not a single drop of
oil can get in or out. They even have
to line up to buy gasoline right in
their own country. Their currency has
become worthless. They are an
international pariah. Not long ago, I
heard a brilliant political scientist
say, "Everyone supports Iran and not us
, not the United States." They might
have said that, but they would be very
happy to see that nation collapse from
within, and that will certainly happen.
The issue is not whether the war is
going badly or well. The issue is that
the war no longer has any meaning. In
other words, our lives continue, while
Iran's do not. And time is on our side;
it may take 6 months, but they cannot
survive the economic sanctions
currently being applied. And the entire
Middle East region is starting to wake
up and realize that there is a very
good opportunity to move toward a
normal regional atmosphere without
authoritarian and cruel governments.
That is indeed the Islamic Republic of
Iran. In particular, the Strait of
Hormuz will no longer have strategic
significance in the next two or three
years. The oil pipelines currently
under construction will bypass the
Strait of Hormuz. And when you look at
the oil situation in the world,
everyone says, "Man, China has the
largest oil storage capacity and it is
full." That is true, but it has its
limits. They are not producing it, they
are just hoarding it, and in fact, they
are helping us indirectly because oil
prices haven't risen. Because China is
currently not participating in the
market, as they haven't touched
Venezuelan or Iranian oil at all. But
when Iran is no longer a concerning
factor, oil prices won't just fall. I
think they will plummet, and who will
control the majority of the world's oil
? That is the United States. Because
the U.S. has this good deal with
Venezuela, and the U.S. is currently
the world's largest natural gas
producer. Ladies and gentlemen, this is
the reason Dan often tells you that
Putin stands no chance when compared to
Trump. Trump is the president of the
world's number one superpower.
Furthermore, Mr. Trump is making
America great again, that is truly the
case. What do you think about the
analysis by Professor Victor David
Hanson and oil tycoon Mikhail
Khodorkovsky? I invite you to help Dan
by leaving your opinions in the
comments section; thank you, and see
you in the next program. Thank you very
much.
